items.title: Hayden Panettiere, ‘Nashville’ and ‘Heroes’ Star, Dies at 36
items.summary:
Hayden Panettiere, the actress and singer who played country star Juliette Barnes on the ABC and CMT drama Nashville, has died at 36. Her representative confirmed the death to ABC News, as Billboard reported, and no cause has been disclosed.

Her father, Skip Panettiere, announced the death in a statement. "It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden," he said, calling her "an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen." He asked for privacy "as our family takes time to process this unimaginable loss."

Panettiere starred on Nashville from 2012 to 2018 opposite Connie Britton, and her work there gave her a substantial recording career. The show's soundtrack series, issued through Big Machine Records, charted consistently; the first installment, The Music of Nashville: Season 1, Volume 1, entered the Billboard 200 at No. 14 and Top Country Albums at No. 4 in 2012 on first-week sales of 56,000 copies. Her tracks as Juliette Barnes, among them "Telescope," "Don't Put Dirt on My Grave Just Yet" and the duet "Wrong Song," found an audience with country listeners, and the role brought her two Golden Globe nominations.

Born in Palisades, New York, in 1989, she worked as a child actor in Ally McBeal, Remember the Titans and Message in a Bottle, and voiced a character in Pixar's A Bug's Life, before breaking through as Claire Bennet on NBC's Heroes in 2006. She signed with Hollywood Records during that run and released the single "Wake Up Call" in 2008. Her later credits included Scream 4, Scream VI, I Love You, Beth Cooper and the TV movie Amanda Knox: Murder on Trial in Italy.

Panettiere spoke openly about growing up famous. She published a memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, in May, and discussed motherhood, mental health and postpartum depression, a subject she took up after realizing "how many people needed to hear it." She shared a daughter, Kaya, with former heavyweight champion Wladimir Klitschko, whom she was with on and off for nine years before their 2018 separation.

Her death follows that of her younger brother, actor Jansen Panettiere, who died in February 2023 at 28.

items.title: Stars Pay Tribute to Hayden Panettiere After Her Death at 36
items.summary:
Actors, musicians and her own union spent the week responding publicly to the death of Hayden Panettiere, who died at 36. Her family confirmed the death on Aug. 17, and no cause has been disclosed. Her father, Skip Panettiere, described his daughter in a statement as "an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen," and asked for privacy.

Among the earliest responses, Billboard reported, was one from Selma Blair, a close friend, who left a series of comments on Panettiere's last Instagram post. "I love you. Don't be gone. Don't be gone. Please. Please," she wrote, adding, "I love you whale tail my friend," and, in another comment, "I'm dying. Please be here."

Jay Shetty, who interviewed Panettiere on his podcast earlier this year, commented on Variety's report of her death: "I can't believe it. Our friendship had just begun and I was so moved by the conversation we shared earlier this year. My love and condolences to her family and fans." Her Scream co-star David Arquette, who appeared with her at a horror convention in February, wrote, "I love you Hayden." Beverley Mitchell of 7th Heaven posted beneath the same item: "Praying the news is wrong! You are such a bright light and soooo loved."

Rosie O'Donnell shared a photo of Panettiere on Instagram with the caption "Oh my god – heartbroken." Jeremy Renner wrote, "Bless you and your family." SAG-AFTRA issued a statement of its own: "We join in mourning the sudden passing of Hayden Panettiere."

The range of the tributes tracked a career that started in childhood and moved through commercials, soap operas, film, network television and music over three decades. Panettiere became internationally known as Claire Bennet on Heroes in 2006 and earned two Golden Globe nominations for Nashville, where she starred from 2012 to 2018. The show's Big Machine Records soundtracks charted regularly on the Billboard 200 and Billboard's country and soundtrack tallies, and "Undermine," her 2012 duet with Charles Esten, reached the Digital Song Sales chart. She had also signed with Hollywood Records at the height of Heroes, releasing "Wake Up Call" in 2008.

Panettiere is survived by her father and her daughter, Kaya. Her brother, actor Jansen Panettiere, died in February 2023 at 28.

items.title: Ariana Grande Brings Out ‘Wicked’ Co-Star Cynthia Erivo for ‘For Good’ and ‘Get Happy/Happy Days Are Here Again’ at London Concert
items.summary:
Ariana Grande brought Cynthia Erivo onstage at London's O2 Arena on Aug. 16, the second night of her U.K. run on the Eternal Sunshine tour. The two Wicked leads performed "For Good" and a medley of "Get Happy" and "Happy Days Are Here Again."

The medley has history for the pair. As Variety noted, they first performed it on a Wicked television special that aired last November, itself a nod to the interlocking arrangement Judy Garland and Barbra Streisand devised for a television appearance in the 1960s.

The Eternal Sunshine tour, named for Grande's seventh studio album, is scheduled to close with 10 dates at the O2, wrapping Sept. 1. After that, Grande plans to withdraw from public-facing work. Her representative told People in early August that she "looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny."

News of the break arrived alongside word that Grande had exited the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim's Sunday in the Park With George, where she had been set to appear opposite fellow Wicked cast member Jonathan Bailey. The scrutiny her camp described has intensified during a long promotional stretch, with commentary online focused on her appearance — including reaction to the video for the title track of her eighth album, Petal, which arrived July 31.

Grande and Erivo played Glinda and Elphaba in Jon M. Chu's Wicked and its sequel, Wicked: For Good, and both received Oscar nominations for the first film. The London residency runs through the start of September.

items.title: Hirokazu Kore-eda, Carol Morley & Lili Horvát In Competition At London Film Festival
items.summary:
The BFI London Film Festival has named the 10 films competing for its top prize, with Hirokazu Kore-eda, Carol Morley and Lili Horvát among the directors in the lineup. The festival runs Oct. 7-18, and the winner will be announced at the LFF Awards on Sunday, Oct. 18.

Kore-eda enters with Look Back, a Japanese coming-of-age story spanning more than a decade about two girls who bond over their ambition to become manga artists. Morley's 7 Miles Out adapts her semi-autobiographical novel about adolescence in Stockport in the 1970s and '80s, following a girl named Ann in the wake of her father's suicide as she finds refuge in the emerging new-wave punk scene. Horvát's third feature, My Notes on Mars, rounds out the trio of headline titles.

The rest of the competition includes Act 3 from Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor, Benjamín Naishtat's Argentine period noir Glaxo, Sergei Loznitsa's archival documentary Imperium, Giovanni Tortorici's Palermo-set Kettic, Rubaiyat Hossain's The Difficult Bride, The Idiot(s) from Malgorzata Szumowska and Michal Englert, and May el-Toukhy's Woman Unknown. Deadline reported that the selection draws from the UK, Ireland, Brazil, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Japan and Poland, and spans fiction and documentary.

Festival director Kristy Matheson framed the slate around the event's anniversary edition. "As we celebrate the 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival, it's an honour to have a number of alumni filmmakers represented in the Official Competition alongside those making their first appearance at the festival," she said, adding that the lineup "brings an astounding array of filmmaking styles to the screen."

Several of the directors have festival histories: Molloy and Lawlor screened Baltimore at LFF in 2023, and Tortorici's debut Diciannove played in 2024, with Luca Guadagnino producing Kettic as well. Naishtat's thriller features a score by Japanese composer Shigeru Umebayashi, and Monica Bellucci plays the mother in Kettic.

Shortlists for the Grierson Award for Best Documentary, the Sutherland Award for Best First Feature and the Short Film Award follow in September, as does the full program. The festival will name its awards juries in the coming weeks.

items.title: Motion Picture Association Inks AI IP Protection Deal With ByteDance
items.summary:
The Motion Picture Association announced Monday that it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with ByteDance covering intellectual property and likeness protections across the Chinese company's generative AI tools and platforms. The deal applies to Seedance, Seedream 5.0 Lite, TikTok, CapCut and Dreamina, among other products.

Seedance is the model behind the fully AI-generated clip of Tom Cruise fighting Brad Pitt that circulated widely roughly six months ago. As the Hollywood Reporter noted, the pattern echoes OpenAI's Sora, which launched last year amid a wave of unauthorized videos featuring recognizable characters and performers before the company scaled back and eventually shut the product down earlier this year. ByteDance has taken the opposite tack, continuing to invest in Seedance, now among the more capable video models alongside Google's offerings.

MPA chairman and CEO Charles Rivkin tied the agreement to the trade group's copyright position. "Today's agreement illustrates our belief that copyright is a cornerstone of the film and television industry and reinforces our commitment to protect creative content," he said, adding that the MPA has had "constructive engagement with ByteDance to implement meaningful guardrails on Seedance and Seedream" over the past several months.

ByteDance general counsel John Rogovin said the company "respects the intellectual property rights that underpin creative industries around the world" and that "responsible innovation in AI goes hand in hand with meaningful protections for rightsholders." He described the MOU as "an important framework for continued collaboration as the technology evolves, across a variety of products and platforms."

Neither side detailed the specific technical measures or enforcement mechanisms the memorandum sets out. The agreement leaves the MPA and ByteDance in an ongoing working relationship on safeguards across the company's generative AI services.
